title: Adaptive headroom policy rewrite and burst fallback sequence for large-tenant reserved pools
creator: Aisha Morgan
description: Customer escalations reported intermittent capacity shortfalls for large tenants during regional traffic spikes. Investigation shows autoscaler hysteresis combined with tenant-weight smoothing delayed headroom allocation and prevented timely burst replenishment. This ticket rewrites headroom/adaptive hysteresis logic, adds a fast-path fallback for burst requests, and coordinates urgent customer comms and mitigations.
root_cause: Telemetry correlated repeated slow scale-ups with the hysteresis window increasing proportionally to recent scale events. For tenants with heavy weight smoothing, the scaler suppressed incremental reservations until several windows passed, causing reserved-pool depletion under microburst load. Additionally, the admission path did not trigger fallback to a pre-authorized burst fallback pool when headroom remained below threshold due to a race in the leadership lease renewal.
mitigation_plan: 1) Roll out emergency config to reduce hysteresis window from 5m to 30s for affected regions. 2) Enable per-tenant temporary emergency headroom grants for 1 hour. 3) Deploy fast-path admission that routes overflow burst traffic to cold-burst fallback pools with controlled token buckets. 4) Patch leadership lease race (PR linked) and backfill telemetry to catch missed scale signals.
rollout_plan: Stage A: Canary runtime-1.19-hotfix-2 on us-east-1 reserved control plane for 2 tenants (BrightMarket, QuasarMaps) for 30m. Stage B: Gradual ramp to 20% of regions with 15m observation windows. Stage C: Global rollout with rollback guard if tail latency increases > 20% or error rate > 1% for 10m.

notes: Design trade-off: reducing hysteresis reduces missed scale-ups but increases oscillation risk; mitigation via short-lived emergency grants and smoothing limits recommended.
Long-term: propose a predictor that anticipates headroom loss by modeling tenant request burstiness and token bucket refill rates rather than relying solely on recent scale history.
Customer follow-ups: prepare tailored post-incident report for BrightMarket and AcmeHealth including token-level cost impact and timeline of mitigations.
